title: Definitive Guide: How to Choose Process Automation in Brazil
summary: Complete guide to choosing the right process automation in Brazil, with practical criteria and no need for IT.
body_markdown:
Choosing process automation in Brazil requires criteria that go beyond any generic market: integration with local ERPs like Omie and Conta Azul, Portuguese-language support, and familiarity with the tax and approval rules used here. This guide brings together the main points for deciding with more confidence.


The Brazilian market has particularities that international tools don't always handle well: date formats, specific tax categorization, multiple company IDs within the same economic group, and an operational culture that still relies heavily on WhatsApp for day-to-day decisions.


Facing so many options, from spreadsheets to full process management platforms, Brazilian managers need clear criteria, not just a list of features.


## What Every Process Automation Needs to Solve


- Reducing repetitive manual tasks, like duplicate typing between systems
- Organizing approvals with clear authorization by amount, cost center, or hierarchy
- Giving real-time visibility into what's pending at each step
- Integrating with the company's ERP, without depending on intermediary tools
- Working for multiple company IDs or branches without multiplying the cost per account


## Practical Criteria for Choosing the Right Platform


- Check whether the integration with Omie or Conta Azul is native, with no Zapier or Make in between
- Assess the real implementation time: minutes rather than months make a difference in the return
- Confirm whether support is in Portuguese and whether the company has an established presence in Brazil
- Prioritize no-code tools, which the team itself can adjust without depending on IT
- Consider per-user billing instead of per company ID, if the company has multiple accounts
- Check security certifications, like SOC 2, before connecting financial data


## Why the Brazilian Context Calls for Its Own Approach


- Local ERPs like Omie and Conta Azul require Brazil-specific formats and categories
- Companies with a holding structure and multiple branches need orchestration across ERP accounts
- WhatsApp is a real operational channel in Brazil, not just a personal messaging tool
- Brazilian teams adopt tools faster when support and content are in Portuguese

## Frequently asked questions


**Why consider criteria specific to the Brazilian market?** Because local ERPs, tax formats, and the use of WhatsApp as an operational channel are particularities found here, exactly why how to choose process automation in Brazil deserves its own guide. See more at[jestor.com](https://www.jestor.com/?ref=blog.jestor.com) .


**Does process automation work for companies with multiple company IDs?** Yes, as long as billing is per user and the platform orchestrates several ERP accounts.


**Do you need to switch ERPs to automate processes?** No. The automation integrates with the existing ERP and organizes what happens before the posting.


**Does process automation handle the company's tax side?** No. It organizes the process and sends the entry to the ERP, which is responsible for the tax side.
